# Tire fitment and suspension geometry

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Stuff the tire into its highest possible position, then step on the slider to compress the suspension. [t747]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Stuff the tire into its highest possible position using a jack or similar tool.
2. Step on the slider (or equivalent) to compress the suspension and simulate full droop.

_Procedure reported by [t747]._

## Tools

- Jack [t747]
- Slider [t747]

## Tips & gotchas

- Mark where contact occurs with a pencil after stuffing the tire. [t747]
- [Partial] Trim small amounts of material at a time until clearance is achieved. [t747]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Assuming a suspension lift provides equal vertical space all around inside the wheel well without accounting for pivot points and secant lines. [t747]
